chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad and Faḍālah, from Abān, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the blood of the Magians, the Jews, and the Christians: is there anything against them and against one who kills them if they deceive the Muslims and manifest enmity and deceit toward them? He said: “No, unless he is one who habitually kills them.”

He said: And I asked him about a Muslim—would he be killed in retaliation for the people of dhimmah and the People of the Book if he killed them? He said: “No, unless he is accustomed to that and does not refrain from killing them; then he is killed while humbled.”

key_terms.الْمَجُوسِ: the Magians, mentioned here as a non-Muslim community
key_terms.دِمَاءِ: bloodshed or legal liability concerning killing
key_terms.صَاغِرٌ: humbled or abased at the time of punishment
key_terms.مُتَعَوِّدًا: one who has made a habit of doing something repeatedly

ai.seo_question: Is a Muslim executed for killing a dhimmi or a member of the People of the Book according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses legal rulings concerning killing members of the Magians, Jews, Christians, and Ahl al-Dhimmah. It states that a Muslim is not ordinarily subject to retaliation for killing them, but if he becomes habituated to such killing and persists in it, he is to be executed as punishment. The report reflects a juridical discussion of qisas and repeated unlawful violence.
